newsitem.title: USA: Hong Kong has world's freest economy - survey.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong has world's freest economy - survey.

text.p: Hong Kong has the freest economy in the world, according to a survey released on Sunday by the Heritage Foundation, a conservative think tank.
The survey, compiled annually, ranks the relative freedom of economies based on 10 factors, ranging from trade and tax policies to regulation and the size of the black market.

Singapore, Bahrain, New Zealand, Switzerland, the United States, the United Kingdom, Taiwan, the Bahamas and the Netherlands round out the top 10, the foundation said. Hong Kong also ranked No. 1 last year.
The survey argues that freer economies tend to outperform fettered ones.
"Our analysis strongly suggests that countries with free-market public policies grow faster than countries that discourage economic freedoms," Heritage Foundation economist William Beach said.
China, which will take over the British colony of Hong Kong in mid-1997, ranked 125th on the index of 148 economies.

Although its economy has been one of the fastest-growing in the world in recent years, the survey's authors argue that that performance cannot be sustained unless the Chinese government reduces its intervention in the economy.
North Korea ranked last on the index.

-- Germany, long considered Europe's economic powerhouse, lost gound to other countries over the last year, partly because of a failure to complete privatisation of state-owned industries. Its economy ranked 20th, down from 15th.
-- Chile surpassed Panama as the freest economy in Latin America, largely because of progress in reducing trade barriers and eliminating price controls. Little progress occurred in Mexico.
-- Japan's ranking was unchanged at No. 11.
-- Africa as a region continued to score poorly.
